CNN, MS NOW and Politico Sue Trump Administration After White House Ban
CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit Monday challenging President Trump’s decision to bar their journalists from the White House, arguing that the restrictions violate their First Amendment rights.
The three news organizations filed the 27-page lawsuit in federal court in Washington, D.C., after their reporters were denied entry to White House grounds over the weekend. Their previously valid credentials were disabled and confiscated following Trump’s announcement Friday that the organizations would no longer be permitted access.
The lawsuit names President Trump, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung, White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Secret Service Director Sean Curran as defendants. The organizations are seeking immediate restoration of their journalists’ access while the broader constitutional challenge moves through the courts.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico argue that the administration retaliated against them because President Trump disapproved of their coverage. They contend that excluding particular organizations based on their reporting amounts to viewpoint discrimination prohibited by the First Amendment.
President Trump announced the ban Friday after repeatedly accusing the three organizations of publishing inaccurate and unfair stories about his administration. He has defended the decision by saying he supports a free press but does not believe the White House should be required to accommodate organizations he considers purveyors of “fake news.”
The White House has taken the position that access to the presidential complex is a privilege rather than an unrestricted right. The administration has rejected accusations that the decision represents a broader attack on press freedom and maintains that the dispute concerns the conduct and coverage of the specific organizations involved.
The dispute escalated further when the major television networks responsible for providing pooled video coverage of presidential events announced they would stop distributing that footage. ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC participated in the move following the restrictions placed on CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
The lawsuit also alleges violations of the Fifth Amendment, arguing that the reporters lost their credentials without adequate notice or an opportunity to challenge the decision. The organizations say the restrictions prevent their journalists from performing the same White House reporting duties available to other credentialed news outlets.
The case has been assigned to U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, who was appointed to the federal bench by President Trump during his first term. The organizations are asking the court for emergency relief that would restore their White House access while the lawsuit proceeds.
The legal battle is the latest confrontation between President Trump and national news organizations over access to his administration. The court will now have to consider whether the White House has the authority to exclude the three organizations under these circumstances or whether the restrictions amount to unconstitutional retaliation based on their journalism.

sources.news_title: 'Blatant violation' of rights: News outlets file lawsuit over Trump ban
sources.text:
(WASHINGTON) — The three news outlets banned from the White House by President Donald Trump on Monday filed a First Amendment lawsuit to restore their access.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico are seeking a temporary restraining order demanding the White House restore their reporters’ credentials after Trump announced the ban on Friday.
In a joint statement on Monday, the three news outlets said the lawsuit aims to “protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes.”
“Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference,” the statement said.
Trump said in a social media post following the news on Monday that the barring of journalists was not “an assault on the Free Press” but instead “an assault on the FAKE NEWS,” which he claimed was a national security “threat.”
Trump said in a post to social media on Friday, “Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America.”
At an event in the Oval Office shortly after he posted his message, the president suggested there may be more restrictions on other outlets. Trump told reporters he supports a free press, but that “you need a fair and honest press.”
“It’s sick. I mean, there’s something wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stuff. Now, if they want to write them, that’s fine. But I don’t have to let them into my, into the people’s house,” Trump said.
Journalists from the three outlets were turned away from the White House over the weekend. A reporter from CNN said on air that she was told by a Secret Service agent that her badge had been deactivated.
The three outlets are challenging the legality of the president’s ban on multiple fronts, according to the lawsuit.
The lawsuit argues the ban violates the outlets’ reporters’ due process rights, that it unlawfully retaliates against their protected speech and that it violates the First Amendment by barring them from a nonpublic forum for unlawful reasons.
“This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles,” the news outlets wrote.
The lawsuit warns of a cascading effect for other news organizations should Trump seek to expand the scope of the ban, as he said he may do in his Friday remarks in the Oval Office.
“The ban is already severely impeding the ability of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO to cover the President and his administration,” according to the lawsuit. “Every day, critically important news is breaking at the White House and in the press pool: President Trump is the commander in chief of a country at war; he is traveling to New York today to address the United Nations General Assembly tomorrow; he is meeting with China’s President Xi Jinping at the White House on Thursday; and he is steering national policy on the ever-advancing technology of artificial intelligence. And the ban inflicts an injury on all news media organizations-who now risk a similar fate if they engage in reporting the President deems insufficiently favorable.”
The five members of the White House TV pool — ABC News, NBC News, CBS News, Fox News Media and CNN — issued a statement on the matter on Monday, saying, “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”
Vice President JD Vance on Monday pushed back on the notion that Trump’s actions constituted a ban, saying that the White House would not provide “special access” to outlets it deems are spreading “propaganda” against the president and his agenda.
“He’s not banning media outlets. What he’s doing is saying we’re not going to give you special access to the White House if you engage in what is effectively propaganda,” Vance said.
Trump’s initial social media post said he was “banning” the news outlets.
Vance was pressed by pool reporters traveling to with him on how this is not an attack on the First Amendment. Vance said the outlets are still able to report on the White House — it’s just that they won’t be able to maintain what he called “special access” to the building.
“Well, they can still report on the Trump White House. They can still get the public reports. They can still, of course, talk to people in the administration and outside the administration. What the president has said is, ‘we’re not going to give you special access inside the White House,"” Vance said.
The civil case has been assigned to D.C. District judge Timothy Kelly, who in 2018 oversaw former CNN correspondent Jim Acosta’s lawsuit that similarly sought to restore his press pass.
At the time, Judge Kelly, a Trump appointee, ruled in Acosta’s favor after finding that the Trump White House did not afford him proper due process in revoking his credentials.
The full D.C. Circuit and the Supreme Court have yet to establish settled precedent in the wake of Trump’s earlier attempted ban on The Associated Press from being part of the press pool and attending certain White House events last year.
While a D.C. District court judge backed the AP, a three-judge panel with the D.C. Circuit put the ruling on hold and later wrote that “restricted presidential spaces are not First Amendment fora opened for private speech and discussion.”
Monday’s lawsuit is expected to cite a 1977 ruling in which the full D.C. Circuit found that the White House cannot arbitrarily deny a journalist a press pass without due process.
“As the D.C. Circuit has long held, the interest that members of the press have in their White House hard passes is ‘protected by the first amendment’ and ‘undoubtedly qualifies as liberty which may not be denied without due process of law under the fifth amendment,"” the attorneys wrote, according to the court papers shared by Politico.
ABC News’ Fritz Farrow and Hannah Demissie contributed to this report.

sources.text:
By Mary McCue Bell (The Washington Times)
A trio of news outlets is suing the Trump administration following their ban from the White House, citing First Amendment violations.
CNN, Politico and MS NOW were barred entry from the White House complex on Friday and subsequently had their reporters’ credentials deactivated and confiscated Saturday.
President Trump said he banned the outlets for intentionally reporting “fake news.”
“This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” the media organizations said in a joint statement Monday morning.
“Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting,” the statement said. “Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference.”
The three alleged in the lawsuit, filed Monday in the U.S. District Court in Washington, that Mr. Trump issued the prohibition simply because “he dislikes the content of their coverage of him and his administration.”
In the suit, the outlets detail the president’s repeated opposition to their coverage of him and his administration, labeling this prohibition both discrimination and retaliation against their work.
Mr. Trump’s statements “make clear he implemented the ban to coerce more favorable coverage of the administration,” the suit reads.
The president’s basis for their ban was a “result of their constant ’reporting’ FAKE NEWS!”
“It’s really just cumulative stories over the last few years. You get sick of it,” Mr. Trump said in the Oval Office Friday. “They’re smart people, but they purposely write negative news.”
In response to the lawsuit, Mr. Trump said that the White House is “not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish.”
“It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America,” he said on Truth Social. “It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”
CNN, Politico and MS NOW argue that the embargo infringes on their First Amendment freedom of speech and news-gathering rights.
“This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles,” the lawsuit reads.
The outlets are asking a judge to quickly rule Mr. Trump’s ban unconstitutional and prevent his administration from enforcing it.
Named in the suit are Mr. Trump, White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung and Secret Service Director Sean Curran.
The three media outlets are not the first to have been banned from the White House.
The Trump administration indefinitely barred AP reporters in February 2025 from restricted press pool events after the news outlet declined to adopt the term “Gulf of America” instead of the Trump-decreed Gulf of Mexico. The core legal battle is still ongoing.
CBS, NBC, ABC, CNN and FOX make up the White House TV pool, alternating coverage of the president’s events and trips. As of Monday, there is no scheduled TV pool, CBS correspondent Weijia Jiang said, meaning Mr. Trump will not have a media crew with him at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
The president has actively pursued multiple high-profile defamation and legal actions against major news organizations.
He filed a multibillion-dollar defamation lawsuit against The New York Times over critical coverage and reporting on his business career and background, which a federal judge is currently considering after refiling.
Mr. Trump filed a $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC regarding an edited 2024 Capitol speech documentary. The two parties appointed a former judge for court-mandated mediation.
He has also pursued legal actions or threats against outlets like The Wall Street Journal and previously secured financial settlements from networks including ABC News.
This article was made available to WMAL via The Washington Times.

White House press pool pushes back after Trump bars three outlets
As President Trump refuses entry to outlets he deems unreasonable, lawsuits have been filed to regain access to the West Wing
Past the first checkpoint to get into the White House, multiple carts filled with camera equipment sat along a fence. Wagons loaded with tripods, cables, mics, and cameras sat just past where they normally would be working at full power. Today, they were turned off and packed away.
Last week, President Donald Trump decided to bar CNN, MS NOW and POLITICO from the White House following reporting he considers “FAKE NEWS.”
Trump, in a post on Truth Social on Monday morning, described his move as “instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS,” which he said has “grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America.”
“It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control,” he wrote on the social media site he owns. “It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”
As a result, all of the major television networks that comprise the television press pool — ABC, CBS, NBC, CNN, and Fox News — suspended their White House TV pool coverage. They decided to no longer send camera crews to cover President Donald Trump’s events.
“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government,” the five White House TV pool networks said in a joint statement Monday. “No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”
POLITICO, CNN and MS NOW filed a lawsuit Monday to immediately restore access for their reporters, who had their credentials confiscated by the Secret Service.
In the White House, there was a noticeable shift in the atmosphere. The Washington Blade is the only LGBTQ news outlet that is part of the White House Press Pool, and was acting as the primary print pooler as the situation unfolded on Monday.
Whispers about who might be kicked from the press pool next could be heard both in the press area of the West Wing, as well as outside the part of the White House dedicated to filming the president’s office. It does not prohibit coverage of counseling or psychotherapy as part of gender-affirming care.

Lawsuit filed Monday challenges White House effort to restrict care

This is not the first time the White House has directly attacked gender-affirming care.

CNN, MS Now, Politico sue Trump over White House ban
The White House, south facing, on June 11, 2026. (Photo by Ashley Murray/States Newsroom)
WASHINGTON — The three news organizations that President Donald Trump has barred from entering the White House filed a lawsuit against the administration on Monday.
CNN, MS Now and Politico wrote in a joint statement the suit is intended “to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes.”
“Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting,” the statement continued. “Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference.”
Trump announced last week on social media that he intended to bar journalists from those three news organizations, airing a years-running grievance that he doesn’t believe their reporting is accurate.
“I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW (who recently changed their name from MSNBC due to lack of viewership and credibility!), and Politico (The recipients of an illegal and ridiculous $8 Million Dollar subscription, an All Time Record, directly from the United States Government, under Crooked Joe Biden, in order to keep them “alive.” Seems like corruption to me!), from the White House as a result of their constant “reporting” FAKE NEWS!” he wrote. “Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America. Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow. Thank you for your attention to this matter! President DONALD J. TRUMP”
First Amendment cited
The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, argued the “ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles.”
The lawsuit says White House reporters from those news organizations had their press passes, which must be scanned to get through a Secret Service screening, deactivated.
The news organizations say the ban violates the due process clause, “retaliates against protected newsgathering and speech in violation of the First Amendment” and that it bars journalists “from a nonpublic forum for unlawful reasons.”
The president’s decision to exclude those reporters from the White House “inflicts irreparable harm to these news organizations,” according to the lawsuit.
“The organizations, whose very purpose is to report national news, depend on individual reporters to gather information firsthand at the White House,” it states. “As a result of the ban, they have lost the ability to perform essential newsgathering at the seat of the Executive Branch, where critically important newsworthy events occur every day.
“The ban irreparably curtails the organizations’ speech—preventing them from being able to publish stories they otherwise would—each day it remains in effect. The ban also impermissibly chills the speech of other news organizations and journalists, who must now balance conducting their constitutionally protected and vitally important work of reporting on the White House against the risk that coverage the President ‘dislike[s]’ will condemn them to the same fate.”
The case was assigned to Judge Timothy J. Kelly, who was nominated by Trump during his first term and confirmed by the Senate in September 2017 following a vote of 94-2.
Kelly scheduled a videoconference hearing for Wednesday to hear arguments over whether to issue a temporary restraining order in the case.
TV network coverage of Trump
Trump wrote on social media on Monday morning that the “White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish.”
“It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America,” he wrote. “It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP”
Major television networks don’t plan to fill in for CNN as the television pool covering Trump on Monday, according to an email the network obtained from Fox News Washington Bureau Chief Bryan Boughton, who chairs the TV pool.
“This follows the White House’s position preventing CNN from fulfilling its assigned pool duties,” Boughton wrote, according to the CNN article. “There will be no replacement pool put in place.”
The White House pool rotation includes reporters from the country’s major news organizations, who attend the president’s public events as well as other events that administration staff restrict to only journalists in the pool.
The television pool provides video footage of those events, while the print pooler’s reports about the president’s comments are emailed to reporters at newspapers and online news outlets.
The limited number of reporters from within the White House press corps who participate in the pool are able to ask the president questions during Oval Office events or other restricted appearances.
States Newsroom’s Washington, D.C. Bureau participates in the print pool rotation as part of its membership in the Regional Reporters Association, which represents local news outlets covering the nation’s capital.

An attorney at a nonprofit that defends the First Amendment doesn’t think President Donald Trump will come out on top in a legal battle with three media outlets he banned from the White House.
But after announcing on Friday his ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico — and the resulting lawsuit against him — the White House told Fox News Digital that Trump isn’t backing down.
“I think the Trump administration will not fare well in court because its action here is blatantly unconstitutional,” predicted Aaron Terr, the director of public advocacy at the Philadelphia-based Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE).
Trump took to TRUTH Social on Friday to announce that employees with the three major media outlets will be banned from White House grounds over “reporting FAKE NEWS. He said they “shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States.”
DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS
Terr says that what media outlets report is not at issue.
“There’s settled precedent that when the White House opens its doors to the press, which it has done, the First Amendment walks in too,” Terr said. “So that means the administration can’t ban reporters from the White House grounds just because it doesn’t like their point of view or thinks their coverage is too negative or critical, and the president in his statements has been crystal clear that this was the exact reason that he banned CNN, MSN, and … Politico from the entire White House grounds.”
Reporters and cameramen with the outlets removed their gear and set up on Pennsylvania Ave. over the weekend and this week continued to film live hits from across the street rather than from their usual spots on White House grounds.
In response to Terr’s assessment, the White House remained defiant about the ban.
CNN FIRES BACK AT TRUMP WHITE HOUSE OVER ATTACKS ON REPORTER, CALLS THEM ‘BENEATH THE OFFICE’
Monday morning, the three news outlets filed a lawsuit against Trump seeking an injunction that would halt the president’s ban temporarily, and asking the court to immediately order the restoration of the media members’ White House credentials.
CNN was scheduled for White House television pool coverage on Monday. Fox News Media, ABC News, CBS News and NBC News, the other press pool networks, announced in a joint statement that they would not take CNN’s place.
“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting,” the pool members said in a joint statement.
Additionally, White House Correspondents’ Association (WHCA) President Jacqui Heinrich of Fox News, released a statement expressing the organization’s support of the outlets.
“Today’s action revoking access for journalists from CNN, POLITICO, and MSNOW violates the First Amendment,” she wrote. “The implications extend beyond these organizations: a standard used to exclude one news outlet because of its coverage could be applied to any outlet in the future.”
“The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinize those elected to power, regardless of whether government officials view it favorably,” she continued. “The WHCA calls on the administration to immediately restore our colleagues’ access.”
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SUBPOENAS NY TIMES JOURNALISTS IN GRAND JURY LEAK PROBE TIED TO AIR FORCE ONE REPORT
Terr said that while nobody has a First Amendment right to report from the White House, he said court precedent established that once a media outlet gains access to the White House, that access cannot be revoked for ideological reasons.
“The principle here is that once the government provides access, it then can’t condition that access on whether you’re expressing a viewpoint that the government agrees with,” he said. “It’s a broader First Amendment principle that the government cannot retaliate against Americans for protected speech, and that includes revoking news outlets’ access to a space open to the press just because the president doesn’t like the actual or perceived slant of their report.”
Terr noted that while there can be bias in media, the alternative of government-controlled media could result in a much worse outcome.

(WASHINGTON) — The three news outlets banned from the White House by President Donald Trump on Monday filed a First Amendment lawsuit to restore their access.

Trump said in a social media post following the news on Monday that the barring of journalists was not “an assault on the Free Press” but instead “an assault on the FAKE NEWS,” which he claimed was a national security “threat.”
Trump said in a post to social media on Friday, “Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America.”
At an event in the Oval Office shortly after he posted his message, the president suggested there may be more restrictions on other outlets. Trump told reporters he supports a free press, but that “you need a fair and honest press.”

Journalists from the three outlets were turned away from the White House over the weekend. A reporter from CNN said on air that she was told by a Secret Service agent that her badge had been deactivated.
The three outlets are challenging the legality of the president’s ban on multiple fronts, according to the lawsuit.
The lawsuit argues the ban violates the outlets’ reporters’ due process rights, that it unlawfully retaliates against their protected speech and that it violates the First Amendment by barring them from a nonpublic forum for unlawful reasons.
“This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles,” the news outlets wrote.
The lawsuit warns of a cascading effect for other news organizations should Trump seek to expand the scope of the ban, as he said he may do in his Friday remarks in the Oval Office.
“The ban is already severely impeding the ability of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO to cover the President and his administration,” according to the lawsuit. “Every day, critically important news is breaking at the White House and in the press pool: President Trump is the commander in chief of a country at war; he is traveling to New York today to address the United Nations General Assembly tomorrow; he is meeting with China’s President Xi Jinping at the White House on Thursday; and he is steering national policy on the ever-advancing technology of artificial intelligence. And the ban inflicts an injury on all news media organizations-who now risk a similar fate if they engage in reporting the President deems insufficiently favorable.”
The five members of the White House TV pool — ABC News, NBC News, CBS News, Fox News Media and CNN — issued a statement on the matter on Monday, saying, “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”
Vice President JD Vance on Monday pushed back on the notion that Trump’s actions constituted a ban, saying that the White House would not provide “special access” to outlets it deems are spreading “propaganda” against the president and his agenda.

Trump’s initial social media post said he was “banning” the news outlets.
Vance was pressed by pool reporters traveling to with him on how this is not an attack on the First Amendment. Vance said the outlets are still able to report on the White House — it’s just that they won’t be able to maintain what he called “special access” to the building.
“Well, they can still report on the Trump White House. They can still get the public reports. They can still, of course, talk to people in the administration and outside the administration. What the president has said is, ‘we’re not going to give you special access inside the White House,"” Vance said.
The civil case has been assigned to D.C. District judge Timothy Kelly, who in 2018 oversaw former CNN correspondent Jim Acosta’s lawsuit that similarly sought to restore his press pass.
At the time, Judge Kelly, a Trump appointee, ruled in Acosta’s favor after finding that the Trump White House did not afford him proper due process in revoking his credentials.
The full D.C. Circuit and the Supreme Court have yet to establish settled precedent in the wake of Trump’s earlier attempted ban on The Associated Press from being part of the press pool and attending certain White House events last year.
While a D.C. District court judge backed the AP, a three-judge panel with the D.C. Circuit put the ruling on hold and later wrote that “restricted presidential spaces are not First Amendment fora opened for private speech and discussion.”
Monday’s lawsuit is expected to cite a 1977 ruling in which the full D.C. Circuit found that the White House cannot arbitrarily deny a journalist a press pass without due process.
“As the D.C. Circuit has long held, the interest that members of the press have in their White House hard passes is ‘protected by the first amendment’ and ‘undoubtedly qualifies as liberty which may not be denied without due process of law under the fifth amendment,"” the attorneys wrote, according to the court papers shared by Politico.

NEW YORK — CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Monday sued President Donald Trump’s administration days after they were barred from covering the White House, calling the selective ban an illegal action and “a blatant violation” of the First Amendment.
The extraordinary ban of the three news outlets' reporters, which began over the weekend, represented a clear escalation of Trump’s long-running efforts — in the courts and through administrative action — to restrict news coverage he finds objectionable or, in his words, “fake news.” They were also the latest test of First Amendment protections in the United States, where the government is constitutionally forbidden from restricting the press.
The Constitution, the banned news outlets said in their lawsuit, “does not allow a president or any other government official to deprive the press of their First Amendment rights and liberty and property interests with no notice or process based solely on his dislike of the content of their reporting.”
The three outlets filed the joint lawsuit two days after their reporters were blocked from the White House and prevented from doing their jobs. The reporters' entry badges were disabled on Saturday, a day after Trump had suddenly announced he was barring the outlets because of reporting he found to be “fake news.”
On Monday morning, the banned TV networks were reporting from an intersection just outside the White House complex. CNN, meanwhile, was removed from its pool duties, which are shared by the five major networks. It had been scheduled to cover the president's trip to New York for the U.N. General Assembly. In an email to members, the TV pool wrote there would be no replacement coverage following the White House actions.
“Effective today, the TV pool will not be covering events designated as pool coverage of the President,” said the email, seen by The Associated Press. “This follows the White House’s position preventing CNN from fulfilling its assigned pool duties. There will be no replacement pool put in place."
CNN's chief White House correspondent, Kaitlan Collins, explained on air that this meant: “When the president does anything today, there will be no TV camera with the president that is broadcasting and sharing this footage" to the viewing public.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit. But on his Truth Social platform, Trump wrote Monday morning that he “cherished” what he called a free press.
“The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish,” the president said in his post. “It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America. It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”
Trump has been more aggressive toward the media in his second term
In his second term, Trump and his Republican administration have upped the ante and punished certain media outlets. Trump has also lashed out at individual reporters in person or over social media, sometimes in strikingly personal terms — insulting them in briefings or in his recent speech at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.
“This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” the outlets said in a joint statement posted early Monday on X.
“Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting," they said. "Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference.”
In the joint complaint, the outlets said: “This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles.”
They say they're being banned from doing their jobs at the White House “for one simple reason: (Trump) dislikes the content of the coverage of him and his administration.”
“President Trump has said in no uncertain terms that he would prefer only to be covered by news organizations and reporters who praise his administration," says the complaint, filed in the name of the three outlets and three correspondents who were denied access Saturday.
It went on: “But the Constitution does not allow a president or any other government official to deprive the press of their First Amendment rights and liberty and property interests with no notice or process based solely on his dislike of the content of their reporting.”
In legal terms, that’s known as “viewpoint discrimination” — the government singling out specific media outlets for the content of what they say or publish. That legal principle is at issue in many of the court cases around Trump’s treatment of the media and would likely be at play this time.
Jameel Jaffer, executive director of the Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University, called the White House move "an attack both on press freedom and the public’s right to independent information about the government.”
"The president’s decision to bar news organizations from the White House for the content of their reporting is a flagrant violation of the First Amendment,” said Jaffer, whose institute is filing a brief to support the lawsuit. The case has been assigned to U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, whom Trump nominated during his first term in the White House.
Reporters were barred Saturday
On Saturday, White House reporters from the two cable networks — Betsy Klein of CNN and Akayla Gardner of MS NOW — went live to report they’d been turned away, their press badges deactivated, when arriving for their jobs at the White House. Soon after, Politico said its White House reporter Cheyenne Haslett was also denied entry and had her badge confiscated.

The move follows the president’s decision last year to bar AP reporters from the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events in retaliation for the news outlet’s decision not to follow his lead in changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico, which lies partially in Mexican and other waters. The AP said it would note when appropriate that Trump had ordered it renamed the “Gulf of America.”

Over the weekend, the AP expressed solidarity with the banned news outlets.

Past presidents have battled with the press, but Trump’s campaign against the media has been unprecedented. He has upended decades of tradition by denying basic access to many major news organizations, launching personal attacks on journalists for their reporting and elevating new media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. During his first term in office, Trump sought to revoke or suspend White House credentials of two correspondents for CNN and Playboy magazine, but federal judges ordered their passes restored.
Trump long has been a critic of the press, rising to fame as a New York real estate developer widely covered in local tabloids, and then as a reality television personality.

NEW YORK (AP)—CNN, MS NOW and Politico said Monday they’ve notified President Donald Trump’s administration they’re filing a joint lawsuit over being denied White House access, saying their First Amendment rights have been violated by the selective exclusion.

They were also the latest test of First Amendment protections in the United States, where the government is constitutionally forbidden from restricting the press.
The three outlets made the announcement in a joint statement posted on X, two days after their reporters were blocked from the White House and prevented from doing their jobs. The reporters’ entry badges were disabled on Saturday, a day after Trump had suddenly announced he was barring the outlets because of reporting he found to be “fake news.”
On Monday morning, the banned TV networks were reporting from an intersection just outside the White House complex

It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”
Trump Has Been More Aggressive Toward the Media in His Second Term
In his second term, Trump and his Republican administration have upped the ante and punished certain media outlets. Trump has also lashed out at individual reporters in person or over social media, sometimes in strikingly personal terms—insulting them in briefings or in his recent speech at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.
“This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” the outlets said in a joint statement posted early Monday on X.
“Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting,” they said. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference.”
The Associated Press reviewed a copy of the court document before it was filed.
In the joint complaint, released by the news organizations, the outlets said: “This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles.”
They say they’re being banned from doing their jobs at the White House “for one simple reason: (Trump) dislikes the content of the coverage of him and his administration.”
“President Trump has said in no uncertain terms that he would prefer only to be covered by news organizations and reporters who praise his administration,” says the complaint, filed in the name of the three outlets and three correspondents who were denied access Saturday.
It went on: “But the Constitution does not allow a president or any other government official to deprive the press of their First Amendment rights and liberty and property interests with no notice or process based solely on his dislike of the content of their reporting.”
In legal terms, that’s known as “viewpoint discrimination”—the government singling out specific media outlets for the content of what they say or publish. That legal principle is at issue in many of the court cases around Trump’s treatment of the media and would likely be at play this time.

All three organizations that were banned covered the White House’s actions extensively during the weekend.
The WHCA’s president, Jacqui Heinrich, called on the Trump administration to immediately restore the three outlets’ access.

The move follows the president’s decision last year to bar AP reporters from the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events in retaliation for the news outlet’s decision not to follow his lead in changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico, which lies partially in Mexican and other waters. The AP said it would note when appropriate that Trump had ordered it renamed the “Gulf of America.”

WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump forcefully defended his decision to revoke White House credentials from three major legacy media outlets on Monday, framing the measure as a defense of national security against coordinated media bias as CNN, MS NOW, and Politico filed a joint federal lawsuit challenging the restriction.
In a statement posted Monday to Truth Social, Trump pushed back against critics who alleged First Amendment violations, arguing that his actions target institutional media bias rather than legitimate press freedom.
“The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish,” Trump wrote. “It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America. It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”
Trump’s post came as CNN, MS NOW, and Politico filed a federal lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia seeking an emergency temporary restraining order to restore their press access. The legal challenge alleges that revoking credentials based on editorial coverage violates the outlets’ First Amendment rights to a free press and their Fifth Amendment due process protections.
The access dispute began Friday when Trump announced the ban, citing dissatisfaction with the outlets’ reporting. By Saturday morning, White House security personnel had deactivated and confiscated hard passes for correspondents from all three organizations, and CNN was removed from the television pool for Trump’s travel to the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Appearing on CNBC’s Squawk Box, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended the administration’s stance, contending that legacy news organizations have lost public trust due to persistent bias and what he described as self-absorbed reporting.
Bessent pointed to instances where he argued press coverage prioritized journalists’ personal experiences over threats against the president, referencing security events surrounding the White House Correspondents’ Dinner and an incident in Ankara.
“I’m sure the press cares more about the press than anything else,” Bessent said. “After the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, they didn’t come in there to kill the press. They came in to kill the president. But all we heard about was the personal experiences of the press people in the room, because somehow they were more important. Same thing with the aircraft in Ankara, that the presidential pool saying, ‘Oh, we were so vulnerable.’ They were there to kill the president of the United States of America. And the Secret Service made a decision.”
Bessent stated that public approval ratings of legacy media has dropped below historical norms due to what he described as widespread public perception of bias.
“Clearly, for the legacy media, the equilibrium is so far out of kilter because what group is one of the few that is less popular than the U.S. Congress? Legacy media, and why is that? sources.text:
CNN, MS NOW, Politico say they’ve notified Trump they’re suing over denied White House access
NEW YORK (AP) — CNN, MS NOW and Politico said Monday they’ve notified President Donald Trump’s administration they’re filing a joint lawsuit over being denied White House access, saying their First Amendment rights have been violated by the selective exclusion.
The administration’s announcement of the bans Friday and the White House’s subsequent actions over the weekend represented a clear escalation of Trump’s long-running efforts — in the courts and through administrative action — to restrict news coverage he finds objectionable. They were also the latest test of First Amendment protections in the United States, where the government is constitutionally forbidden from restricting the press.
The three outlets made the announcement in a joint statement posted on X, two days after their reporters were blocked from the White House and prevented from doing their jobs. The reporters’ entry badges were disabled on Saturday, a day after Trump had suddenly announced he was barring the outlets because of reporting he found to be “fake news.”
On Monday morning, the banned TV networks were reporting from an intersection just outside the White House complex
Also Monday, CNN was removed from its pool duties, which are shared by the major networks. It had been scheduled to cover the president’s trip to New York. In an email, the TV pool, which consists of the five major networks, wrote that there would be no replacement coverage following the White House actions.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit, which was expected to be filed later in the morning. But on his Truth Social platform, Trump wrote Monday morning that he “cherished” what he called a free press.
“The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish,” the president said in his post. “It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America. It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”
Trump has been more aggressive toward the media in his second term
In his second term, Trump and his Republican administration have upped the ante and punished certain media outlets. Trump has also lashed out at individual reporters in person or over social media, sometimes in strikingly personal terms — insulting them in briefings or in his recent speech at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.
“This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” the outlets said in a joint statement posted early Monday on X.
“Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting,” they said. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference.”
The Associated Press reviewed a copy of the court document before it was filed.
In the joint complaint, released by the news organizations, the outlets said: “This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles.”
They say they’re being banned from doing their jobs at the White House “for one simple reason: (Trump) dislikes the content of the coverage of him and his administration.”
“President Trump has said in no uncertain terms that he would prefer only to be covered by news organizations and reporters who praise his administration,” says the complaint, filed in the name of the three outlets and three correspondents who were denied access Saturday.
It went on: “But the Constitution does not allow a president or any other government official to deprive the press of their First Amendment rights and liberty and property interests with no notice or process based solely on his dislike of the content of their reporting.”
In legal terms, that’s known as “viewpoint discrimination” — the government singling out specific media outlets for the content of what they say or publish. That legal principle is at issue in many of the court cases around Trump’s treatment of the media and would likely be at play this time.
Reporters were barred Saturday
On Saturday, White House reporters from the two cable networks — Betsy Klein of CNN and Akayla Gardner of MS NOW — went live to report they’d been turned away, their press badges deactivated, when arriving for their jobs at the White House. Soon after, Politico said its White House reporter Cheyenne Haslett was also denied entry and had her badge confiscated.
All three organizations that were banned covered the White House’s actions extensively during the weekend.
The WHCA’s president, Jacqui Heinrich, called on the Trump administration to immediately restore the three outlets’ access.
“The implications extend beyond these organizations: a standard used to exclude one news outlet because of its coverage could be applied to any outlet in the future,” Heinrich said. “The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinize those elected to power, regardless of whether government officials view it favorably.”
The move follows the president’s decision last year to bar AP reporters from the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events in retaliation for the news outlet’s decision not to follow his lead in changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico, which lies partially in Mexican and other waters. The AP said it would note when appropriate that Trump had ordered it renamed the “Gulf of America.”
The AP filed suit and the case is ongoing. Since returning to office, Trump has pursued other legal action against a variety of different outlets, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the BBC. His administration is also involved in a long-simmering confrontation involving ABC over renewal of its broadcast licenses.

sources.text:
MS NOW, CNN and Politico announced Monday that they are suing President Donald Trump’s administration for banning reporters’ White House access.
Trump said in a Friday Truth Social post that the three news outlets would be immediately blocked from accessing the White House for writing “FICTION and LIES” about his administration. MS NOW, CNN and Politico’s lawsuit seeks to stop the ban and immediately restore White House press access and credentials for the outlets’ reporters. (RELATED: Famous Comedian Absolutely Loses It Over Trump Calling Reporter ‘Piggy’)
“The President banned CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO, and the individual reporters covering the news for those media organizations, in disregard of the most basic guarantees of the First Amendment and the Due Process Clause,” according to the lawsuit. “He did so expressly for the improper purpose of retaliating against Plaintiffs for past news coverage because he deemed it ‘negative’ and chilling future reporting about him and his administration’s policies and actions.”
“This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles,” the suit claims.
The complaint also alleges that the ban is “already severely impeding the ability of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO to cover the President and his administration.”
The case was assigned to U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, who Trump appointed in 2017, NBC News reported.
— POLITICO Press (@POLITICOPress) September 21, 2026
Additionally, the lawsuit claims that CNN, MS NOW, Politico “and their journalists have liberty and property interests in their press credentials and the access those credentials afford to the White House grounds to report on” Trump and his administration.
“This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” Politico, CNN and MS Now said in a joint statement provided to the Daily Caller News Foundation. “Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference.”
The White House did not immediately respond to the DCNF’s request for comment.
Trump claimed in a Monday Truth Social post that the White House “is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish.”
“It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America,” he added in the post.

CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued President Donald Trump and other members of his administration on Monday for banning them from White House grounds, saying it violated their rights to free speech and a free press under the US Constitution’s First Amendment.
The news outlets are seeking a temporary restraining order to block Trump’s action in federal court in Washington and could see emergency hearings in the case as soon as this week.

sources.news_title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico Sue White House as Trump Defends Press Access Ban
sources.text:
CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit Monday seeking restoration of their White House credentials as President Donald Trump argued that his administration is targeting what he calls “fake news,” not freedom of the press.
By yourNEWS Media Newsroom.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit Monday challenging President Donald Trump’s decision to bar their journalists from the White House, escalating a dispute over presidential press access into a First Amendment court fight.
The three news organizations filed their case in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia and asked for a temporary restraining order that would restore their journalists’ access while litigation proceeds. They contend the administration revoked credentials because of objections to their coverage and did so without adequate notice or due process.
“This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” CNN, MS NOW and Politico said in a joint statement.
The organizations said their credentials were revoked “without notice or process” because the White House objected to their journalism. The lawsuit argues that selectively excluding news organizations because of their reporting amounts to unconstitutional viewpoint discrimination.
Trump responded Monday by rejecting the characterization that his administration was attacking press freedom.
“The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish,” Trump wrote Monday. “It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America.”
Trump described reporting he considers false as “corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control,” and said it represents “a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”
The president has not publicly provided evidence establishing that the three organizations coordinated false reporting or that their journalism constitutes a national security threat. Reuters reported that Trump’s Monday statement offered no substantiating evidence for that assertion.
The legal confrontation began after Trump announced Friday that CNN, MS NOW and Politico would be prohibited from the White House “effective immediately.” He accused the organizations of repeatedly publishing “FICTION and LIES” about him, his administration and the United States.
Speaking with reporters later Friday, Trump made clear that he intended the prohibition to extend broadly across White House access.
“I don’t want them in my office. I don’t want them here,” Trump said.
Asked how far the restriction would extend, he replied that it would go “as far as you can.”
Trump separately argued that although the country needs a free press, he believes news organizations should provide what he considers fair and truthful reporting. He said his decision resulted from what he described as a pattern of negative coverage over the previous two years.
The administration began enforcing the president’s directive Saturday. Journalists working for all three organizations were denied entry to White House grounds after their credentials were deactivated or confiscated.
The organizations subsequently signaled that they would challenge the decision in court, culminating in Monday’s joint lawsuit.
The case centers on the extent of the president’s authority to control access to White House facilities and whether access can be withdrawn from otherwise credentialed journalists because officials object to their reporting.
The dispute follows previous court battles over White House press credentials during both of Trump’s administrations.
In 2025, the Associated Press sued after the administration restricted its access to certain presidential events because the organization continued using the name Gulf of Mexico in its reporting while acknowledging Trump’s order renaming it the Gulf of America.
A federal district judge initially ruled that the government could not punish the AP based on its editorial choices. A divided federal appeals panel later allowed the administration to maintain restrictions involving limited-access settings such as the Oval Office and Air Force One while the litigation continued. The full appeals court subsequently declined to overturn that decision.
Trump also faced a White House credential dispute during his first administration involving CNN correspondent Jim Acosta.
The White House revoked Acosta’s press credential in 2018 following a confrontation at a presidential news conference. CNN sued, and a federal judge ordered the administration to temporarily restore the credential while finding that the government had not afforded Acosta sufficient due process. The White House subsequently returned his credential.
The current litigation goes further by challenging the exclusion of three entire news organizations rather than the suspension of a single correspondent.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico are seeking immediate restoration of access as the federal court considers their broader constitutional claims. The administration, meanwhile, maintains that the action is directed at journalism Trump regards as false rather than at the constitutional protection of a free press.
The disagreement now places before a federal judge competing claims over White House authority and First Amendment protections, with the news organizations arguing that presidential officials cannot condition press access on whether the administration approves of their coverage.

- CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are suing President Trump and his administration for banning them from the White House, claiming it violates their First Amendment rights.
- The lawsuit seeks to challenge the ban, which the news organizations argue threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism.
- Trump defended the ban, labeling the media as a security threat and asserting that it is necessary to combat what he calls 'fake news.'
WASHINGTON, DC, USA – CNN, MS NOW and Politico said on Monday, September 21, they are suing President Donald Trump and other members of his administration to protect their rights under the US Constitution’s First Amendment after he banned the news outlets from the White House building grounds.
The three news organizations said they have notified the government that they were filing their lawsuit in the US District Court for the District of Columbia and could see emergency hearings in the case as soon as this week.
“Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference,” they wrote in a joint statement.
The lawsuit aims “to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” they added.
The First Amendment protects the freedom of the press and speech.
Representatives for the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Trump first announced his action on Friday, September 18, in a social media post. The Republican president defended the ban in another social media post on Monday after the lawsuit was announced, calling the news media a security threat, without providing any evidence.
“The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish. It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS,” Trump wrote. “It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”
His administration has upended decades of tradition in dealings between the White House and press, denying the access many major news organizations have had to the president while elevating new media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. He has also filed a number of lawsuits against news organizations.
CNN had been scheduled to cover Monday’s White House events for the broader press corps, including Trump’s trip to New York for the United Nations General Assembly. It was not immediately clear what television footage of the president would be provided to the public.
“The ban is unconstitutional and should be immediately restrained,” the news outlets said in a copy of their lawsuit, adding that the ban was already impeding coverage that could have wider impact.
“The ban inflicts an injury on all news media organizations — who now risk a similar fate if they engage in reporting the President deems insufficiently favorable,” the three wrote in their complaint, which seeks a temporary restraining order to block Trump’s action.
‘A free and independent press’
Trump’s latest move comes as his fellow Republicans seek to defend their narrow majorities in Congress in the November midterm elections as polls show the public souring on Republicans and Trump’s own approval ratings stand near historic lows.
On Saturday, September 19, all three outlets said their journalists were turned away from the White House grounds and their press credentials confiscated, a day after Trump initially announced his ban in a social media post and threatened to block other outlets.
MS NOW and CNN over the weekend instead set up their journalists across the street from the White House and continued to broadcast coverage.
Trump on Friday addressed what he called his “ban on the free press” with reporters at an event in the Oval Office and said there was no particular incident that provoked the move. Asked what other news organizations could be targeted, Trump cited The New York Times and The Washington Post as “fake news” but said they had not been removed yet.
The Associated Press, the White House Correspondents’ Association and others have criticized Trump’s ban, citing the fundamental American right to free speech and calling for access to be immediately restored.
“The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinize those elected to power, regardless of whether government officials view it favorably,” the correspondents’ association said in a statement.
The AP filed its own lawsuit after being barred, along with Reuters, in 2025 from the group of reporters that cover the president’s daily movements.
During his first term in office, Trump sought to revoke or suspend White House credentials of two correspondents for CNN and Playboy magazine, but federal judges ordered their press passes restored. – Rappler.com

CNN, MS NOW and Politico said Monday they’ve notified President Donald Trump’s administration they’re filing a lawsuit over being denied White House access, saying their First Amendment rights have been violated.
The administration’s announcement of the bans Friday and the White House’s subsequent actions over the weekend represented a clear escalation of Trump’s long-running efforts — in the courts and through administrative action — to restrict news coverage by liberal journalists. They were the latest test of First Amendment protections in the United States.
The three outlets made the announcement in a joint statement posted on X, two days after their reporters were blocked from the White House. The reporters’ entry badges were disabled on Saturday, a day after Trump had suddenly announced he was barring the outlets because of “fake news” reporting. On Monday morning, CNN was removed from its pool duties, which are shared by the major networks.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment early Monday over the lawsuit, which was expected to be filed later in the morning.
Trump has been more aggressive toward the media in his second term
In his second term, Trump and his Republican administration have upped the ante against liberal media outlets. Trump has also lashed out at individual reporters in person or over social media, sometimes in personal terms.
“This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” the outlets said in a joint statement posted early Monday on X.
“Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting,” they said. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference.”
In the joint complaint, which was released by the news organizations before being filed later Monday, the outlets say: “This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles.”
They say they’re being banned from doing their jobs at the White House “for one simple reason: (Trump) dislikes the content of the coverage of him and his administration.”
“President Trump has said in no uncertain terms that he would prefer only to be covered by news organizations and reporters who praise his administration,” says the complaint, filed in the name of the three outlets and three correspondents who were denied access Saturday.
“But the Constitution does not allow a president or any other government official to deprive the press of their First Amendment rights and liberty and property interests with no notice or process based solely on his dislike of the content of their reporting.”
In legal terms, that’s known as “viewpoint discrimination” — the government singling out specific media outlets for the content of what they say or publish. That legal principle is at issue in many of the court cases around Trump’s treatment of the media and would likely be at play this time around.
Reporters were barred Saturday
On Saturday, White House reporters from the two cable networks — Betsy Klein of CNN and Akayla Gardner of MS NOW — went live to report they’d been turned away, their press badges deactivated, when arriving for their jobs at the White House. Soon after, Politico said its White House reporter Cheyenne Haslett was also denied entry and had her badge confiscated.
All three organizations that were banned covered the White House’s actions extensively during the weekend.
The WHCA’s president, Jacqui Heinrich, called on the Trump administration to immediately restore the three outlets’ access.
“The implications extend beyond these organizations: a standard used to exclude one news outlet because of its coverage could be applied to any outlet in the future,” Heinrich said. “The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinize those elected to power, regardless of whether government officials view it favorably.”
The Associated Press contributed to this article
